english_translation: It is raining heavily outside there today.

dialogue.shona: Mvura iri kunaya zvakanyanya kunze uko nhasi.
dialogue.english: It is raining heavily outside there today.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Mvura [water / rain] • iri [iri] • kunaya [to / at naya] • zvakanyanya [zvakanyanya] • kunze [outside / outdoors] • uko [uko] • nhasi [today]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('zvakanyanya')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'zvakanyanya' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Actions Happening Right Now: The '-ri ku-' Progressive
grammar_notes.content: To describe an action that is happening right now ('I am doing', 'it is raining', 'they are walking'), Shona uses the helper verb '-ri' ('am/is/are') followed by 'ku-' ('to') and the action verb. For people, the forms are 'ndiri ku-' (I am), 'uri ku-' (you are), 'ari ku-' (he/she is), 'tiri ku-' (we are), and 'vari ku-' (they are). In fast speech or writing, the two words are sometimes joined together (e.g., 'ndiri kuenda' or 'ndirikuenda').
grammar_notes.rule: [Subject + -ri] + ku-[verb] -> Ndiri kuverenga (I am reading) | Vari kufamba (They are walking) | Mvura iri kunaya (It is raining)

grammar_notes.title: Talking About Location: 'pa-', 'ku-', and 'mu-' ('kunze')
grammar_notes.content:
Look at how location is expressed with 'kunze'. Instead of separate prepositions like 'on', 'to', or 'in', Shona attaches one of three location prefixes directly to the front of a noun:
• 'pa-' means 'at' or 'on' a specific point or surface (e.g., 'patafura' = on the table, 'pamusika' = at the market, 'pasi' = on the ground).
• 'ku-' means 'to', 'from', or 'at' a general destination (e.g., 'kuchikoro' = to school, 'kumusha' = to the rural home, 'kubasa' = at/to work).
• 'mu-' means 'inside' an enclosed space (e.g., 'mumba' = inside the house, 'muguta' = in the city, 'mumugwagwa' = in the road).
grammar_notes.rule: pa- = on / at a point (patafura) | ku- = to / at a place (kuchikoro) | mu- = inside (mumba)

cultural_notes.title: Farming ('Kurima'), Rain & the Harvest Season
cultural_notes.content: Agriculture plays a central role in Zimbabwean life, and the arrival of the rains ('mvura') around November marks the beginning of the planting season ('zhizha'). Families cultivate their fields ('munda') using hand hoes ('badza'), rakes ('mahara'), and shovels ('mafoshoro') to grow maize, groundnuts, and vegetables. A plentiful rainfall brings hope for a bountiful harvest ('goho guru'), which is a frequent topic of friendly daily conversation.

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Baba vari mumba asi vana vari kutamba panze.'
options: Mother went to the market to buy fruit and vegetables.
The books and keys are lying on the table.
Father is in the house, but the children are playing outside.
We are going to the rural home tomorrow morning.
active_exercises.correct_answer: Father is in the house, but the children are playing outside.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Baba vari mumba' = 'Father is in the house', 'asi' = 'but', 'vana vari kutamba panze' = 'the children are playing outside'.

active_exercises.prompt: Which locative word means 'in the kitchen'?
Translate this new sentence into English: 'Vana vari kudzidzira kunyora bvunzo kuchikoro.'
options: The children are practicing to write examinations at school.
The teacher gave us new books yesterday morning.
My grandmother grows groundnuts and maize at the rural home.
My friend called me after finishing work today.
active_exercises.correct_answer: The children are practicing to write examinations at school.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Vana vari kudzidzira' = 'The children are practicing', 'kunyora bvunzo' = 'to write exams', 'kuchikoro' = 'at school'.
